Print a Fitted G2Gcov Model

Source: R/methods.R
print.G2Gcov.Rd

Displays a formatted summary of a G2G model fit returned by G2G_static_MLE (time-invariant covariates) or G2G_varying_MLE (time-varying covariates), including convergence status, log-likelihood, AIC, and a parameter table with standard errors and Wald confidence intervals at the fitted confidence level.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'G2Gcov'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted model object of class "G2Gcov".

digits

Integer. Number of decimal places to print. Default 4.

...

Further arguments passed to or from other methods (unused).

Value

Invisibly returns x.

Details

Both fitting functions return an object of class "G2Gcov", and this one method prints either. It only relies on the elements the two have in common: par, par_stderr, par_lower, par_upper, value, convergence, and optional level. If any of the standard errors or confidence limits are missing or NA (the fitting functions return NA when the Hessian at the optimum is singular or not positive definite), they print as NA and a note is added below the table.

See also

G2G_static_MLE, G2G_varying_MLE

Examples

# \donttest{
  data(kb_data)
  kb_data$status <- 1L - kb_data$censor
  fit <- G2G_varying_MLE("Surv(week, status) ~ coupon + anyp",
                          data = kb_data, subject = "id")
#> Warning: The Hessian at the solution is not positive definite (or could not be inverted), so standard errors and confidence intervals are NA.
  print(fit)
#> G2G Model Fit
#> ---------------------------------------------------- 
#> Convergence:       Converged (code 0)
#> Log-likelihood:    -5612.1808
#> AIC:               11232.3616
#> Parameters:        4
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>                Estimate Std.Error Lower.95 Upper.95
#> r (shape)     2996.6875        NA       NA       NA
#> alpha (rate) 40722.0679        NA       NA       NA
#> coupon         -78.2544        NA       NA       NA
#> anyp             0.0020        NA       NA       NA
#> 
#> Note: some standard errors are NA (the Hessian at the optimum is singular or not positive definite).
# }
